chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Bashir Al-Kunasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There may be love for Allah and His Messenger, and love for the world. So whatever is for Allah and His Messenger, its reward is upon Allah; and whatever is for the world, it is nothing.

key_terms.فَلَيْسَ بِشَيْ‏ءٍ: It is nothing / It is insignificant
key_terms.فِي اللَّهِ: For Allah / In the cause of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between love for Allah and love for the world in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the spiritual taxonomy of love (hubb), distinguishing between altruistic devotion to the Divine and its Messenger versus self-centered attachment to worldly pursuits. In Shia scholarship, this distinction underscores the necessity of purifying one's affections (tazkiyah) to ensure that emotional bonds serve as a means to draw closer to Allah rather than becoming a distraction. The Imam’s statement implies that while worldly love is not inherently sinful, it lacks the eternal weight and divine recompense characteristic of love rooted in faith.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn BiN Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Bashir Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There may happen to be love regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup> and love regarding the world. So whatever was regarding Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, so its Reward is upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>; and whatever was regarding the world, so it is not with anything’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Bashir al-Kannasi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Sometimes love is for the sake of Allah and the Messenger of Allah and sometimes it is for the sake of worldly matters. For love, which is for the sake of Allah and the Messenger of Allah, the reward is with Allah. For love that is for the sake of worldly matters there is nothing.”
